title: Structural Results on the Unfair 0-1 Polynomial Conjecture
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A $0$-$1$ polynomial is a polynomial whose coefficients are all either $0$ or $1$. The unfair $0$-$1$ polynomial conjecture states that if $f$ is a $0$-$1$ polynomial and $f(x)=g(x)h(x)$ is a factorisation into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients, then $g$ and $h$ must themselves be $0$-$1$ polynomials. We call $f$ fair if every such factorisation has this property, and unfair otherwise. In this paper, we study structural properties of possible unfair factorisations and obtain conditions which guarantee fairness. In particular, we prove that if $$ f(x)=x^{n-\operatorname{deg} w}w(x)+v(x), $$ where $v$ and $w$ are $0$-$1$ polynomials and $v$ is fair, then $f$ is fair whenever $$ n\geq\max\{\operatorname{deg} w+2\operatorname{deg} v,\,2\operatorname{deg} w\}. $$

title: Two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems for high-dimensional data: noncentral normal-reference inference
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14598v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study noncentral normal-reference inference for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems. Within the Gaussian reference, a shifted null law is accurate if and only if covariance-weighted signal energy is negligible relative to the trace of the squared covariance. We establish the sharp uniform fourth-root error order over unrestricted spectra and a linear bound under spectral spread. A separate spectral-range criterion determines when signal magnitude alone suffices. An augmented spherical reference gives finite-sample calibration for Gaussian samples and asymptotically recovers Gaussian-reference local power under projection fourth-moment bounds and control of diagonal fluctuations, without a dimension-to-sample-size restriction. For unknown Gaussian covariance, explicit trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds turn the linear approximation bound into a simultaneous, computable certificate over local effect ranges. Eigenspace signal energies describe directional power, while a two-point argument limits estimation of unknown local power. Simulations with 10,000 evaluation replications per configuration examine unequal and noncommuting covariances, severe sample imbalance, non-Gaussian observations and the informativeness of the certificate.

title: Universal Invariants for $\gcd(n^k-1,n!-1)>1$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For integers $k\geq2$ and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $S_k^{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}:=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\}:\gcd(n^k+\lambda_1,n!+\lambda_2)>1\}$. This family arose from a MathOverflow problem concerning the existence of integers $n$ satisfying $\gcd(n^2+1,n!+1)>1$ and from the subsequent question of whether arbitrarily many, but finitely many, solutions can be obtained by varying the exponent and the signs. We concentrate on the case $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=-1$ and introduce the notion of a universal invariant for an odd prime $p$, namely an integer $n\geq2$ such that $\gcd(n^{p\cdot m}-1,n!-1)>1$ for every integer $m\geq1$. We prove that this condition is equivalent to $\gcd(n^p-1,n!-1)>1$, characterize the possible prime divisors in terms of roots of unity over finite fields, and recall an explicit construction due to Jonathan Love that yields a universal invariant for every odd prime $p\geq5$, with the cubic case treated separately. As an application, we prove that $|S_k^{-1,-1}|\geq\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ for every integer $k\geq2$, where $\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ denotes the number of distinct odd prime divisors of $k$. Hence, the cardinalities of these sets are unbounded as $k$ varies. This lower bound is deliberately coarse and constructive, as it is obtained by considering only universal invariants; stronger general lower bounds are obtained by different constructions. We also discuss minimal universal invariants, their persistent common divisors, the special structure of the cubic case, and a heuristic due to Will Sawin suggesting that there may be infinitely many cubic universal invariants, although the known examples are exceptionally sparse. Whether $S_k^{-1,-1}$ is finite or infinite for any fixed exponent $k\geq3$ remains an open problem.

title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14645v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),\rho(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $\rho$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

title: Fundamental Limits of Honest Inference with Heterogeneous Transfer Sources
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transfer learning can improve precision by borrowing information from external sources, but how much improvement is possible while maintaining valid inference? We address this by studying honest confidence intervals for a target parameter using multiple sources with heterogeneous prespecified discrepancy bounds. Under local information and admissibility conditions, we establish a universal lower bound on interval length for procedures maintaining uniform coverage. A scalar information equation characterizes the bound, revealing how precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies. Large source samples need not yield greater precision gains when their discrepancies are large. When discrepancies are unrestricted, honest intervals cannot improve upon the target-only rate, even when all sources are unbiased. For the Gaussian location model, we calculate optimal source weights and construct honest intervals attaining the lower bound order, establishing sharpness. We extend the lower bound theory to semiparametric models through parametric submodels. For the Cox proportional hazards model, we verify the information conditions under which the lower bound applies, including under right censoring.

title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14715v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14735v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(\beta_c(n)=\beta_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(\gamma_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/\beta_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
authors: Tania Roa, Meryem Slaoui, Soledad Torres
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The multivariate breeder's equation $\Delta ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\infty\lambda_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $\lambda_n$, such that $\lambda_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_k\lambda_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks
authors: Matteo Bernab\`e, Leonardo Spampinato, David L\'opez-P\'erez, Nicola Piovesan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.

title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation.
  Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14790v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14807v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.

title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14812v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.

title: A family of alternating projection examples whose Ces\`aro means fail to converge strongly
authors: Heinz H. Bauschke, Tran Thanh Tung
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14829v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004. He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved.
  We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Ces\`aro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.

title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14831v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras.
  The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices.
  Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined.
  Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.

title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
authors: Thomas Stark, Georg K\"ostenberger, Nina D\"ornemann
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14836v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

title: Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming in Polynomial Time
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14837v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Lenstra showed that mixed-integer linear programming can be solved in polynomial time when the number of integer variables is fixed and the number of continuous variables is arbitrary. Mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) can be solved in polynomial time when the total number of variables is fixed. However, since MIQP is NP-hard already without integer variables, the analog of Lenstra's result fails unless P = NP. Hence, polynomial-time algorithms for MIQP with an arbitrary number of continuous variables must exploit additional structure. We study MIQPs with two-stage structure, which underlies Benders decomposition and two-stage stochastic programming. A few linking variables, including all integer variables, are coupled with many blocks of continuous variables that interact only through them, both in the constraints and in the objective. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for MIQP with an arbitrary quadratic objective when the number of linking variables and the block size are fixed, while the number of blocks, and hence the number of variables, is arbitrary. The case with no blocks is MIQP in fixed dimension. None of our assumptions can be dropped. Unless P = NP, the number of linking variables and the block size must both be fixed, the blocks cannot interact or contain integer variables, and large blocks cannot be allowed even if their objective is linear. Unless FPT = W[1], the exponent of the running time must depend on both the number of linking variables and the block size.

title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

title: A Novel Iterative Algorithm Incorporating Machine Learning for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck Equations in Three-Dimensional Ion Channel Simulation
authors: Yuyan Ao, Benzhuo Lu, Shi Shu, Ying Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14866v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. But its convergence efficiency highly depends on the selection of the relaxation parameter, unsuitable parameters will lead to slow convergence or even divergence. At present, parameter selection relies heavily on manual experience, which is inefficient and unstable, significantly hindering the solving efficiency for practical problems such as ion channel simulations. To address this, we propose a machine learning-based parameter selection method, which can select near-optimal relaxation parameters for the Gummel iteration of PNP equations for ion channels. Based on the machine learning-based parameter selection algorithm, we develop a coupled finite element and Gummel iteration solver, and more stable convergence and higher computational efficiency have been achieved in ion channel simulations. To validate the method, we conduct tests on two real channels with complex geometries that differ significantly from the training samples. Numerical results demonstrate that this method has a significant effect on improving the convergence efficiency and stability of Gummel iteration, confirming its applicability in practical ion channel simulations.

title: A Master Identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14874v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for $1/\pi$, and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.

title: Message-Passing-Based Bayesian Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Pilot-Guard-Free AFDM
authors: Yuan Zhengdao, Guo Qinghua, Jin Ming, Liu Zilong, Xiao Pei
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing channel estimation methods for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) over doubly dispersive channels commonly isolate pilots and data with pilot guard symbols, resulting in substantial transmission overhead, while fractional Doppler introduces off-grid mismatch and complicates accurate channel estimation. This paper develops a pilot-guard-free AFDM transmission and reception scheme with a Bayesian receiver for joint channel estimation and data symbol detection. Uniformly interleaved pilots are embedded among data symbols without dedicated guard symbols, and the resulting pilot-data coupling is explicitly incorporated into the joint inference problem rather than suppressed through guard-based isolation.

title: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions
authors: Xiangjian Zhang, Shanyin Tong, Xiaofeng Xu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14883v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.

title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization
authors: Wanqi Hou, Yanzhen Peng, Chao Ding
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

title: The optimization landscape of robust high-dimensional mean estimation: stability, moment adaptation, and mirror descent reweighting
authors: Roberto I. Oliveira, Zoraida F. Rico, Philip Thompson
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only $p\ge2$ moments, bounded by $\nu_p$. We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,\nu_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

title: Weight-Adjusted Entropy-Stable BR2 and CDG Viscous Discretizations with Wall Boundary Conditions for Compressible Flows on Curvilinear Grids
abstract:
arXiv:2611.14994v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin schemes are known for their robustness. These schemes satisfy a semi-discrete entropy inequality, mimicking the entropy inequality of the continuous governing equations. Entropy-stable viscous discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions have been used in the literature, using a scheme similar to BR1. On the other hand, viscous discretizations with compact stencil, such as BR2 and CDG schemes, are more efficient for computation and for forming the Jacobian. Moreover, it is known that the weight-adjusted formulations have better efficiency with regard to the computational and storage costs. To that end, we derive the weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG schemes with modifications for the numerical flux at the boundary to account for the entropy-stable boundary conditions.

title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent for the integrated density of states
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15014v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.

title: Multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for incompressible flow: second-order consistency and parameter selection
authors: Yuyang Xu, Yuxuan Zhang, Jin Zhao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15033v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct and analyze multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two and three space dimensions. The same moment-space relaxation matrix is applied to all physical components, with independent rates for the flux, stress, and energy moments. A Maxwell expansion organized by moment parity establishes formal second-order consistency of the unforced interior schemes under diffusive scaling, assuming a smooth near-equilibrium Maxwell branch. The viscosity depends only on the flux rate; for the two-dimensional scheme, we identify the first contributions of the stress and energy rates to the second-order macroscopic truncation error. We further construct a positive definite symmetrizer for the collision Jacobian at rest and derive an exact weighted-norm identity for the nonlinear kinetic residual under local collision. At fixed viscosity, a finite Fourier search selects the free rates by combining transverse-mode accuracy with short-wavelength damping. The resulting rates are compared with those calibrated against flow errors on a coarse grid. Numerical experiments exhibit second-order convergence and illustrate how the free rates affect spectral properties and finite-time flow errors.

title: RPX: Certifying Agent-Generated MILP Reformulations at Scale
authors: Haozhen Bai, Wenjie Zhu, Qian Hu, Caihua Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15035v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present RPX, an independent certificate checker for AI-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). RPX verifies that every feasible solution of either the original or the reformulated model can be converted into a feasible solution of the other with no worse objective value. This guarantees equal optimal values and enables solution recovery in the original variables. The checker derives the required checks directly from both models and verifies the certificate using exact arithmetic and reusable reconstruction rules. RPX certifies an agent-generated reformulation for each of the 240 instances in MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2. The source models contain up to 27.3 million matrix nonzeros. The median time to decode and check a certificate is 0.312 s, with a 95th percentile of 10.1 s.

title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
authors: Wonsik Yoo, Hoon Lee, Seok-Hwan Park
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15054v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

title: Frank-Wolfe Theorems for Mixed Integer Quadratic Optimization
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15055v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Frank-Wolfe theorem states that a quadratic function bounded from below on a polyhedron attains its infimum. We study when this remains true in the presence of integer variables, for sets defined by quadratic inequalities. Our main result is a complete classification for sets defined by convex quadratic inequalities with rational coefficients and a rational affine hull, a condition that holds for all full- dimensional sets. One integer variable never destroys attainment: if every rational quadratic objective that is bounded from below attains its infimum over the set, even after adding rational linear constraints, the same holds with one integer variable. In dimension at most 2, integer variables never destroy attainment. In dimension at least 3 and with two or more integer variables, attainment holds for every such objective if and only if the set has bounded curvature, that is, it is bounded except along directions in which all constraints are linear. Without convexity, these results remain valid, except that bounded curvature is no longer necessary. Moreover, integer variables can destroy attainment only if there are at least two of them and at least one continuous variable. The result for one integer variable follows from a lifting theorem, which also extends known results for cubic objectives and convex polynomial constraints. Finally, for convex constraints and rational data, attainment holds when the objective is bounded from above, convex, or quasi-convex over a full-dimensional convex set containing the feasible region.

title: Relative-energy stabilization of an irreversible port-Hamiltonian tubular reactor
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.

title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15098v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls.
  For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
authors: Alessandro Chiesa, Guy Weissenberg, Eylon Yogev, Kai Zhe Zheng
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15128v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius.
  We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=\rho n$, fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrt{\rho}+\eta)n\rceil$, with error $O_{\rho,\eta}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding.
  For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{\rho,\eta}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{\rho,\eta,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $\rho,\eta,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15129v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method for Mean Field Games on Scattered Point Clouds
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15132v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. Each row combines a positive generalized finite difference Laplacian with a nonnegative decomposition of the drift along rays to surrounding visible neighbors, with mirror images at reflecting walls, and every fixed-policy matrix is an M-matrix for arbitrary cell-P\'eclet number. We prove a discrete comparison principle and, on polygons with re-entrant corners included, that one HJB solve at a prescribed density converges to the viscosity solution off the boundary vertices, for convex Hamiltonians of at most quadratic growth under a structure condition. On a two-room floor plan with re-entrant door jambs, the computed HJB solutions converge to exact ones. A source-free exact MFG tests the fully coupled computation. At matched degrees of freedom on a grid domain, the meshfree HJB solve has a larger $L^2$ error and a smaller $L^\infty$ error than a five-point finite-difference solve, and is about twice as expensive including the stencil construction. On a non-convex evacuation game, the interior nodes of nine clouds receive monotone rows, apart from a few next to the boundary vertices that copy a neighbor.

title: Subgradient and Stochastic Finite-Difference Methods for Constrained Strongly Quasiconvex Optimization
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15144v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a projected subgradient method for solving quasiconvex minimization problems. By employing the Clarke subdifferential, we prove that the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm converges to a solution of the minimization problem when the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous and strongly quasiconvex in the sense of Polyak, under the same assumptions required for convex functions with the convex subdifferential. Moreover, we derive explicit convergence rate estimates for both the iterates and objective function values. In particular, compared with the corresponding results for nonsmooth, locally Lipschitz, strongly convex optimization, our analysis replaces strong convexity with strong quasiconvexity while preserving the order of the convergence rate, thereby extending the guarantees to a class of possibly nonconvex objective functions. In addition, we investigate a stochastic finite-difference scheme for minimizing a strongly quasiconvex function subject to inequality constraints defined by strongly quasiconvex functions, and establish a convergence rate of order $O(k^{-1/4})$, consistent with known complexity bounds for stochastic zeroth-order methods.

title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner \cite{FL24,FL25}.

title: On Star Monotone Operators: Theory and Applications
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15151v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Introduced by Solodov and Svaiter \cite{SS}, star monotone operators have repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition ensuring global convergence of first-order algorithms, without requiring full monotonicity. Yet, despite this recurring role, a systematic study of the class itself has been missing from the literature. This paper fills that gap with the first comprehensive treatment of star monotone operators, a class that strictly encompasses monotone and pseudomonotone operators with nonempty zero sets, together with operators that are strongly quasimonotone along rays and satisfy a radial nondegeneracy condition. We develop basic calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and precise structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions. We further demonstrate the versatility of star monotonicity through a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, applications to Minty and Stampacchia variational inequalities, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operators related to the Debreu--Koopmans problem.

title: Robust High-Order BUG Integrators without Basis Augmentation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation without basis augmentation or rank truncation. The basis and core updates use the same approximate increment. We establish a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate that controls the error in the low-rank approximation by the increment error. Under the stated assumptions on the vector field and its normal component, sufficiently accurate increments yield local and global error bounds whose constants and step-size restrictions are independent of small singular values. Using explicit Runge--Kutta increments, we obtain robust orders two, three, and four for the explicit midpoint method, Heun's third-order method, and Merson's fourth-order method, respectively. Every internal stage and final approximation has rank at most the prescribed rank $r$. We also prove that these orders are retained under arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-$r$ SVD truncation at the internal stages and the endpoint, without a separate assumption on the truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence orders and show comparable performance with and without augmentation.

title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15182v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
authors: Seraphin F. Kimaryo, Jung-Mo Moon, Kyungchun Lee
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15199v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
authors: Oliver Gaul, Tim Donkiewicz, Marco L\"ubbecke
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

title: Zero-Hopf Networks
authors: Manuela Aguiar, Ana Dias, Fahimeh Mokhtari
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15221v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15233v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

title: Higher order schemes for the numerical solution of integro-differential equation-based age-of-infection models with time-dependent contact rates
authors: Anna Wendler, Jan Hasenauer, Martin J. K\"uhn
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging.
  Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.

title: Exact Decisions and Certified Values in $L_\infty$-Norm Computation from State-Space Representations
authors: Alban Quadrat, Fabrice Rouillier, Grace Younes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15258v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computing the $L_\infty$-norm of a time-invariant linear ordinary differential control system is a routine task in robust control, usually delegated to floating-point routines that perform well on most practical systems. Behind the numerical value, however, lies a discrete decision: whether a pole lies on the imaginary axis, and whether a mode of a realization is actually a pole of the transfer matrix. Floating-point arithmetic can only replace this decision with a tolerance. This paper explains, for a control audience, what reliable symbolic-numeric computation offers for this problem: exact arithmetic where a decision has to be made, and certified enclosures where a value has to be computed. We show how the problem is turned into a small polynomial system directly from state-space data, how this system is solved in practice, and what it costs. A benchmark on the {\tt COMPleib} library and on families of systems with known norms shows that two standard numerical routines err in opposite directions on the imaginary-axis decision, and never on the same system, while the certified method decides it correctly on every instance tested and computes the norm at a cost comparable to that of the numerical routines on most systems. We conclude with practical guidelines for users of numerical tools.

title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis and Computation
authors: Jing Zhang, Mohammed Al Kobaisi, Dmitry Ammosov, Jian Huang, Yunqing Huang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.15275v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.
